s: Wir wollen gehen, aber immer eure Finger auf dem Mund, ich bitte euch: Die Zeit ist aus ihren Fugen gekommen; o! unseliger Zufall! daß ich gebohren werden mußte, sie wieder zurecht zu sezen!
And still your fingers on your lippes I pray, / The time is out of ioynt: Oh cursed spight, / That euer I was borne to set it right.
The Art of Fugue (musical work by Johann Sebastian Bach)
Fuge.et: From Italian fuga, itself borrowed from Latin fuga.

fügen.et:
From Middle High German füegen, fuogen, from Old High German fuogen, from Proto-West Germanic *fōgijan, from Proto-Germanic *fōgijaną, from Proto-Indo-European *peh₂ḱ- (“to join, attach”).
Cognate with Dutch voegen and dated English fay, which is related to En…

s: right, justification (for acting a certain way)
ich hab weder fug noch vrsach gehabt / gemelten seinen Bericht anzufechten
I had neither right nor cause / to challenge the report of the aforementioned
Fug.et: Inherited from Middle High German vuoc (“propriety, that which is opportune”).
